sources.title: The Prose Edda: Gylfaginning
sources.author: Snorri Sturluson
sources.kind: primary text in historical English translation
verifiedFacts: Freyja receives half of the slain in Folkvangr; she rides in a cat-drawn chariot.
Freyja seeks the travelling Odr and weeps red-gold tears. The passage names her Brisingamen.
limits: A medieval literary record, not a single exhaustive account of all Norse religion.
The passage does not establish that Brisingamen is amber.
No HP debt, revival, copied skill, or speed-exchange game mechanic is stated.

sources.title: The Younger Edda
sources.author: Snorri Sturluson
sources.kind: primary text in historical English translation
verifiedFacts: Loki borrows Freyja's falcon-guise in the Idunn rescue narrative.
limits: Spellings and chapter divisions differ from other translations.
Action-order exchange is a creative adaptation, not a claimed mythical power.
sources.editionNote: The fetched Gutenberg e-text is based on the 1901 Scott, Foresman and Company printing; the copyright page gives 1879. The e-text transcriber explicitly distinguishes the original 1879 book and the 1901 printing.

sources.title: Thrym's Poem (Þrymskviða)
sources.author: D. L. Ashliman, University of Pittsburgh
sources.edition: Retelling based on Olive Bray, The Elder or Poetic Edda (1908), pp.126–137; revised 2009-11-20
sections: Freyja lends the feathered coat; Loki flies to Jotunheim
sources.kind: university-hosted retelling with stated source edition
verifiedFacts: Freyja lends a feathered coat that Loki wears.
limits: This page is a retelling, not a literal translation of the Old Norse poem.

sources.title: Fishing at Iwaya on Enoshima
sources.author: The Cleveland Museum of Art
sources.kind: museum collection interpretation of Japanese reception
verifiedFacts: The description associates Benzaiten with water, music, and entertainment in the Japanese Enoshima setting.
limits: This is evidence for Japanese reception/iconography, not an ancient Sanskrit textual episode.
It does not license treating all Sarasvati and Benzaiten traditions as identical.
HP redistribution is an original design metaphor.
